ket_qua.statement: About 150 years ago Santa Cruz del Islote was a small uninhabited island that fishermen from Cartagena and Tolú used to rest and to shelter from storms.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: NatGeo (2017), citing photographer Charlie Cordero who documented the island, says that about 150 years ago it was an uninhabited patch of land used by fishermen from Cartagena and Tolú to rest and shelter from storms. BBC Mundo (2018) dates the settlement to 1870 (about 150 years). The rest-and-shelter detail has only one reputable source, so attribution is advisable.
ket_qua.de_xuat: GIU statement; optional light hedge in narration: 'About a hundred and fifty years ago, the story goes, this was a bare little island...'

Colombia: cómo es vivir en Santa Cruz del Islote (BBC Mundo)

ket_qua.statement: Colombia's Ministry of Housing held meetings on a drinking-water project for Santa Cruz del Islote in which solar-powered seawater desalination was considered as a solution.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The Ministry of Housing's SINAS minutes (Acta 1, 7 Oct 2020; Acta 2, 20 Oct 2020) record reverse-osmosis desalination plants 'dotadas de celdas fotovoltaicas de energía solar' presented for El Islote and agree that solar panels should power the plant and pumping. This text came from search-indexed excerpts because WebFetch returns only the SINAS page title. Separately, the Consejo de Estado ruling records a desalination plant proposal by Aguas de Cartagena and orders the Ministry to design drinking-water programmes for the island.

ket_qua.statement: Residents of Santa Cruz del Islote enlarged their island by hand with coral and other materials, rely on drinking water delivered by boat, and face flooding and erosion from the sea.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The Consejo de Estado ruling (2026) cites the Navy carrying water to the island 'por medio de un bongo', orders weekly drinking-water shipments, records a risk inspection finding 'inundaciones que han afectado sus viviendas', and finds that 'la corriente marina produce erosión'. Noticias RCN (Nov 2020, hurricane Iota) quotes a leader saying 'tenemos el mar dentro de las casas'. BBC Mundo and RCN say the island was built by hand on coral.

ket_qua.statement: Fishing and tourism are the two pillars of the economy of Santa Cruz del Islote; tourism is becoming increasingly important.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: Phiên chính mở La Nación 31/7/2026 (bài của El País): 'El turismo está cobrando un rol cada vez más protagónico en la economía ... aunque su principal sustento sigue siendo la pesca.' Bỏ chữ 'fast' khỏi statement (vòng 2 khong-ro vì 'growing fast'). Lời đọc 'Fishing and tourism keep a lot of families here going' không nói tốc độ tăng.

ket_qua.statement: Residents of Santa Cruz del Islote stay close to their fishing grounds, earn growing income from tourism, and belong to families that have lived on the island since it was settled roughly 150 years ago.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: La Nación 2026: đánh cá vẫn là sinh kế chính, du lịch ngày càng quan trọng; 'Los orígenes de este asentamiento ... se remontan a finales del siglo XIX', 'generación tras generación'. NatGeo: khoảng 150 năm; BBC Mundo: 1870. Vòng 2 khong-ro chỉ vì cụm 'growing income from tourism' không được định lượng; La Nación nói 'con el crecimiento del turismo'.
